headline: Crowds are manageable with strategic positioning and timing
summary: Migration hotspots, especially Mara River crossings during August peak, attract significant vehicle density (15-40 vehicles at popular crossing points). Crowds can be reduced by: visiting shoulder months (June, late October), staying in private concessions with vehicle limits, positioning at less-known crossing points, or adjusting expectations. Peak crowds are the trade-off for peak migration.

assumptions.text: August is peak migration month with highest crowds and prices.
Private concessions enforce vehicle limits, reducing vehicle competition at sightings.
June and late October offer migration with 40-60% fewer vehicles.

gains: Shoulder months: Migration present with significantly fewer vehicles
Private concessions: Vehicle limits ensure exclusivity
Remote crossing points: 5-10 vehicles vs 30+ at popular points
Northern Serengeti: Generally fewer crowds than Mara
losses: Shoulder months: Slightly lower crossing probability
Private concessions: Premium pricing (2-3x national park camps)
Remote points: May require longer drives or mobile camping
Avoiding August means missing peak probability window

change_conditions: If crowds are unacceptable, visit June or late October instead of August.
If budget allows, private concessions provide crowd control.
If willing to work harder, remote crossing points reward effort.
If crowds are acceptable trade-off, August delivers highest crossing probability.
